Mayor Zohran Mamdani will announce on Monday the rebranding of the NYPD’s controversial Strategic Response Group as he faces pressure from his lefty allies to ban the elite tactical unit.

Mamdani promised to get rid of the SRG during his mayoral campaign after activists for years complained about the way in which the unit handled protests.

Hizzoner is slated to say he’s “decoupled” the 500-strong police unit’s duties of responding to demonstrations from its counterterrorism tasks, insiders briefed on the plans told The Post.

The hastily cooked-up ploy is meant to appease the far-left wing of his party — which has recently loudly advocated for Mamdani to make good on his campaign promise to disband the SRG, sources said.

Mamdani will pitch the move as a “massive overhaul” of how the city deals with First Amendment-protected gatherings in the city — but insiders claimed the announcement would have little-to-no effect on the ground.

Sources described it as more of a revamp in which the SRG will continue operating under a different name, and still respond to active shooters and other potential mass casualty or terrorism-related events.

“This is not a disband, this a rebrand,” said one city official.

One of the only substantive changes put forward by the administration will be the addition of a slate of civilian workers who will work under the Mayor’s Office of Community Safety, which currently only has two employees.

The workers, who have yet to be hired or trained, will respond to protests to attempt to de-escalate alongside officers in the NYPD’s Community Affairs Bureau, which already responds to the overwhelming majority of demonstrations.

“That is like at least a year out,” one source predicted.

The civilians will not respond to protests without armed officers, according to the insiders.

If protests turn violent, additional officers could be called in to make arrests, but it wasn’t immediately clear from which units.

The SRG historically has responded to demonstrations when they turn violent and can only be deployed with the sign off of the mayor. It has only handled such events fewer than 20 times this year and made around a dozen arrests.

Mamdani additionally plans to announce a ban on kettling — a police tactic to encircle protesters, which became controversial during the 2020 George Floyd protests — and tear gas.

Both are already being banned in the patrol guide.

The attempt at a splashy move comes after his comrade, congresswoman-elect Darializa Avila Chevalier, attacked the Mamdani administration over the handling of a protest after ICE agents shot a Dominican migrant in the city.

She pushed for the SRG to be disbanded, setting off a firestorm among fellow Democratic Socialists of America members, who joined the calls.

Mamdani campaigned on the pledge but after taking office, the complicated process was not prioritized.

He put the project on the “back burner,” and then scrambled to come up with a response to the backlash, The Post reported last week.

The announcement is not expected to be an executive order, sources said.

news.content: در نتایج جستجوی خود، پوشش خبری بیشتر ما را مشاهده کنید. شهردار زوهران مامدانی روز دوشنبه در حالی که با فشار متحدان چپ‌گرای خود برای ممنوعیت این یگان تاکتیکی نخبه مواجه است، تغییر نام گروه واکنش استراتژیک بحث‌برانگیز پلیس نیویورک را اعلام خواهد کرد. مامدانی در جریان مبارزات انتخاباتی شهرداری خود، پس از سال‌ها شکایت فعالان از نحوه برخورد این یگان با تظاهرات، وعده داد که SRG را منحل کند. افراد مطلع از این برنامه‌ها به The Post گفتند که قرار است شهردار بگوید وظایف واحد پلیس 500 نفره را که شامل واکنش به تظاهرات می‌شود از وظایف ضدتروریسم آن «جدا کرده» است. منابع گفتند این ترفند که به سرعت طراحی شده است، قرار است جناح چپ افراطی حزب او را که اخیراً به شدت از مامدانی خواسته است تا به وعده انتخاباتی خود مبنی بر منحل کردن SRG عمل کند، آرام کند. مامدانی این اقدام را به عنوان «بازنگری گسترده» در نحوه برخورد شهر با تجمعاتی که تحت حمایت متمم اول قانون اساسی هستند، معرفی خواهد کرد — اما افراد مطلع ادعا کردند که این اعلامیه تأثیر کمی بر شرایط میدانی خواهد داشت یا اصلاً تأثیری نخواهد داشت. منابع آن را بیشتر به عنوان یک تغییر ساختاری توصیف کردند که در آن SRG با نامی متفاوت به فعالیت خود ادامه خواهد داد و همچنان به تیراندازی‌های فعال و سایر حوادثی که احتمالاً منجر به تلفات جمعی یا مرتبط با تروریسم می‌شوند، واکنش نشان خواهد داد. یکی از مقامات شهر گفت: «این منحل شدن نیست، بلکه تغییر نام است.» یکی از تنها تغییرات اساسی که توسط دولت پیشنهاد شده است، افزودن گروهی از کارمندان غیرنظامی است که تحت نظر دفتر ایمنی اجتماعی شهردار کار خواهند کرد، دفتری که در حال حاضر تنها دو کارمند دارد.

The state’s education chief is pushing Gov. Kathy Hochul and Albany pols to cough up an expected massive funding increase for school districts to comply with her controversial move to KO the Regents.

The tin-cup pitch from Commish Betty Rosa could trigger a battle with Hochul, who has been critical of phasing out the state’s Regents exams, which New York high school students have been required to pass to graduate.

“When we have an initiative like this, we can’t be starved,” Rosa said during a Board of Regents meeting this week, referring to her push to replace the exams with alternative graduation requirements — and the need to train teachers to achieve her demand.

“This state has to make a huge investment if we’re going to modernize and transform education,” she said without specifying how much money she would request from Hochul and the state legislature.

Her department declined to comment to The Post.

The Regents exams, which students have needed to pass in math, English, science and Global Studies to obtain a diploma, became a graduation requirement during former Gov. George Pataki’s tenure and under then-state Education Commissioner Richard Mills.

The Board of Regents, with Rosa’s backing, voted in September to make the exams optional — meaning kids wouldn’t have to take them if they didn’t want to — as the panel worked to develop alternative graduation requirements that could include student projects or portfolios.

But the federal government recently stepped in and is requiring the kids to at least still take the exams, regardless of what New York does with the results, according to the Albany Times Union.

Beginning in 2028, New York high school students will no longer be required to pass the exams to finish high school.

The state’s graduation policy is set by the 17-member New York Board of Regents, whose members are appointed by Democrats who control the legislature.

The governor does not have a direct role in appointing the Regents, but Hochul has enormous power over school funding and has passed laws she wanted that impact education, such as banning cellphones during the school day.

“The Governor’s priority remains ensuring all New York students receive a high-quality, rigorous education,” a Hochul rep said in an emailed response to Rosa’s comments. “Details of the Executive Budget will be released in January.”

The Times Union first reported that Rosa would seek additional state funding to help establish new graduation standards and train educators to implement them.

Teachers across the state will need experts to instruct them on how to grade portfolios and other projects students must pass for graduation, a more challenging task than easy-to-grade Regents exams.

Rosa said every school may need a coach to help master the new graduation standards.

“We can’t keep using the excuse, ‘They’re not ready,’” Rosa said of districts.

Last year, the Regents board requested a $1.1 billion increase in school funding for various projects.

Hochul said she should have more say over education policy, including graduation requirements. But the education department is not under her purview.

“People see in the articles, ‘New York state abandons Regents,’” Hochul said recently on the Max Politics Podcast. “They think I’m New York.

“The buck should stop with me, given that we are the funder of education.”

Hochul’s fellow Democrats control the Assembly and Senate, and she would have to wage a potentially nasty fight with them to stop or reverse the Regents board’s decision to scrap state exams as a graduation requirement, sources said.

Pataki, governor from 1995 to 2006, told The Post in September that “getting rid of the Regents is incredibly stupid.

“It seems like the Education Department’s main function right now is to disguise the fact that too many New York state schools are failing to educate our kids,” the former gov said.
news.content: پوشش خبری بیشتر ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. رئیس آموزش و پرورش ایالت در حال فشار آوردن به فرماندار کتی هوچول و سیاستمداران آلبانی است تا افزایش قابل توجه بودجه مورد انتظار برای مناطق آموزشی را تأمین کنند تا با اقدام بحث‌برانگیز او برای حذف آزمون Regents مطابقت داشته باشد. درخواست کمک مالی از سوی کمیسر بتی رزا می‌تواند باعث درگیری با هوچول شود، که از حذف تدریجی امتحانات Regents ایالتی انتقاد کرده است؛ امتحانات Regents برای فارغ‌التحصیلی دانش‌آموزان دبیرستانی نیویورک الزامی است. روزا در جلسه هیئت امنای این هفته با اشاره به تلاش خود برای جایگزینی امتحانات با الزامات جایگزین فارغ‌التحصیلی — و نیاز به آموزش معلمان برای تحقق خواسته خود — گفت: «وقتی چنین طرحی داریم، نمی‌توانیم از نظر مالی دچار مشکل شویم.»او بدون اینکه مشخص کند چه مقدار پول از هوچول و قوه مقننه ایالتی درخواست خواهد کرد، گفت: «اگر می‌خواهیم آموزش را مدرن و متحول کنیم، این ایالت باید سرمایه‌گذاری عظیمی انجام دهد.» وزارتخانه او از اظهار نظر برای The Post خودداری کرد. امتحانات Regents که دانش‌آموزان برای اخذ دیپلم باید در دروس ریاضی، انگلیسی، علوم و مطالعات جهانی قبول شوند، در دوران تصدی فرماندار سابق جورج پاتاکی و تحت مدیریت کمیسر آموزش و پرورش وقت ایالت، ریچارد میلز، به یکی از الزامات فارغ‌التحصیلی تبدیل شد. هیئت مدیره، با حمایت رزا، در ماه سپتامبر رأی داد که امتحانات اختیاری شوند — به این معنی که اگر بچه‌ها نخواهند، مجبور نباشند در آنها شرکت کنند — زیرا این هیئت در حال تلاش برای تدوین شرایط جایگزین برای فارغ‌التحصیلی بود که می‌توانست شامل پروژه‌ها یا نمونه‌کارهای دانش‌آموزان باشد.

news.originalContent:

Mayor Zohran Mamdani crowed Friday that New York City now complies with the state’s mandate to reduce public school class sizes — but it only happened after he begged for an extension and his administration tweaked the math.

Hizzoner and Schools Chancellor Kamar Samuels announced that 73.4% of Big Apple public school classes now comply with the class-size law, “surpassing” the 70% compliance target for the 2026-27 school year.

The law requires all New York City classrooms to have no more than 20 to 25 students, depending on grade level, by the 2029–30 school year.

The limits are set at 20 students for K-3rd grade, 23 for grades 4 to 8 and 25 for high school.

The Mamdani administration successfully pushed for a two-year extension after Samuels admitted in March that the mandate would be “very difficult” to meet by the 2027–28 school year.

The state also reduced the compliance target this year to 70%, down from the original target of 80%.

In addition to the decreased target and extension, which weren’t mentioned in City Hall’s self-congratulatory press release, the city also quietly changed its math to hit compliance.

On page seven of the Department of Education’s report, it admits that this year’s count included “cluster” classes — like gym, music or tech classes that aren’t taught by their usual teacher.

“NYCPS updated its data reporting capabilities and infrastructure to include cluster classes to further support compliance with the law,” the November report states.

Without the tricky tweak, the Big Apple would have only hit a 69.5% compliance rate under previous years’ counts, Samuels told Chalkbeat, which first reported the news.

The report also states that exam prep courses at the middle and high school level were added into this year’s count.

Meanwhile, despite Hizzoner’s administration bragging about its $244 million investment to hire teachers to comply with state law, the Big Apple has 500 fewer teachers than last year’s total of 69,900.

Enrollment in New York City public schools plummeted by nearly 22,000 last year alone in its steepest decline since the pandemic, according to an October Comptroller report.

The Big Apple has lost a whopping 187,000 students since the 2013-14 school year, the comptroller report also found.

City Hall and the NYC Department of Education did not respond to requests for comment.
news.content: در نتایج جستجوی خود، پوشش خبری بیشتر ما را مشاهده کنید. شهردار زوهران مامدانی روز جمعه اعلام کرد که اکنون شهر نیویورک از دستور ایالت برای کاهش تعداد دانش‌آموزان در کلاس‌های مدارس دولتی پیروی می‌کند — اما این اتفاق تنها پس از آن افتاد که او درخواست تمدید مهلت کرد و دولت او در محاسبات دست برد. شهردار و کامار ساموئلز، رئیس مدارس، اعلام کردند که 73. در حال حاضر 4 درصد از کلاس‌های مدارس دولتی شهر نیویورک از قانون تعداد دانش‌آموزان در کلاس پیروی می‌کنند و از هدف 70 درصدی پیروی از این قانون برای سال تحصیلی 26-2027 «فراتر رفته‌اند». این قانون مقرر می‌کند که تا سال تحصیلی 30-2029، در تمام کلاس‌های شهر نیویورک، بسته به پایه تحصیلی، حداکثر 20 تا 25 دانش‌آموز حضور داشته باشند. این محدودیت‌ها برای پایه‌های K تا سوم 20 دانش‌آموز، برای پایه‌های چهارم تا هشتم 23 دانش‌آموز و برای دبیرستان 25 دانش‌آموز تعیین شده است. پس از اینکه ساموئلز در ماه مارس اذعان کرد که دستیابی به این هدف تا سال تحصیلی 2027-28 «بسیار دشوار» خواهد بود، دولت مامدانی با موفقیت برای تمدید دو ساله این هدف فشار آورد. همچنین دولت امسال هدف انطباق را از هدف اولیه 80% به 70% کاهش داد. علاوه بر کاهش هدف و تمدید مهلت، که در بیانیه مطبوعاتی خودستایانه شهرداری ذکر نشد، شهرداری همچنین به آرامی محاسبات خود را تغییر داد تا به انطباق برسد. در صفحه هفت گزارش اداره آموزش و پرورش، این اداره اذعان می‌کند که شمارش امسال شامل کلاس‌های «گروهی» — مانند کلاس‌های تربیت بدنی، موسیقی یا فناوری که توسط معلم معمول آنها تدریس نمی‌شوند — بوده است. «NYCPS قابلیت‌های گزارش‌دهی داده‌ها و زیرساخت خود را به‌روزرسانی کرد تا کلاس‌های خوشه‌ای را نیز شامل شود و از این طریق، بیشتر از شرکت در کلاس‌ها حمایت کند.»

Los Angeles City Hall turned into an ’80s nostalgia fest Friday as punk rock legend Billy Idol and his longtime guitarist Steve Stevens packed the council chamber for a rock ‘n’ roll celebration before taking the party outside for a concert on the Spring Street lawn.

Councilwoman Monica Rodriguez declared Nov. 13 Billy Idol Day in Los Angeles, honoring the British rocker whose spiky platinum-blond hair, signature sneer and rebellious anthems helped define the MTV generation.

“So few artists have left a mark on rock and roll quite like Billy Idol,” Councilwoman Monica Rodriguez told the packed City Hall crowd, praising the punk icon’s decades-long influence on music.

“If you don’t love the ’80s, something’s wrong with you,” she joked before the packed chamber.

Born William Michael Albert Broad in England, Idol first made his mark in the late 1970s as the frontman of the punk band Generation X before launching a solo career that turned him into an international superstar.

After moving to New York in the early 1980s, Idol teamed up with Stevens, whose blistering guitar riffs helped create the sound behind hits including “White Wedding,” “Rebel Yell,” “Eyes Without a Face” and “Dancing with Myself.”

His music became a fixture on MTV, while albums including Billy Idol, Rebel Yell and Whiplash Smile cemented his place in rock history.

Idol, who has called Los Angeles home since 1987, credited the city with helping him fulfill a childhood dream.

“A large part of my music has been made here, always written here,” Idol told council members. “Los Angeles has helped me to fulfill that.”

The 70-year-old rocker also made clear he has no plans to leave his adopted hometown.

“Some people kept telling me to move, and I’m still here,” Idol joked.

Stevens, a Grammy-winning guitarist who also performed on the Top Gun anthem and Michael Jackson’s “Dirty Diana,” recalled how his partnership with Idol began just nine miles from City Hall.

He remembered Idol knocking on his hotel room door with a demo of “White Wedding,” a song they would soon perform at the Central, the Sunset Strip club later renamed the Viper Room.

“What a great day for rock and roll. What a great day for Billy Idol. Or Billy Effing Idol, as you would say,” Stevens joked.

Idol also poked fun at receiving the honor on Friday the 13th.

“We’re gonna make that lucky,” he quipped.

The celebration then spilled out of City Hall and onto the Spring Street lawn, where Idol and Stevens performed a concert, bringing a blast of rock nostalgia to the heart of Los Angeles government.

USC women’s basketball was supposed to arrive in Greenville, South Carolina, Friday, for their highly touted matchup against the Gamecocks, Sunday.

But the team was grounded in Los Angeles following the Federal Aviation Administration’s nationwide ground stop for all U.S. airports.

UPDATE: We have been grounded in Los Angeles following the nationwide ground stop, per the FAA.Will provide updates as we have them.

The team social media account provided the following statement over the unexpected mishap: “We have been grounded in Los Angeles following the nationwide ground stop, per the FAA. Will provide updates as we have them.”

The USC football team has arrived in Bloomington ahead of Saturday’s matchup against Indiana at Memorial Stadium.

Sean Duffy, U.S. Secretary of Transportation, announced Friday that the FAA issued a “nationwide ground stop for all U.S. airports,” which has impacted travel for several sports teams heading to games over the weekend.

USC women’s basketball is one of several collegiate or professional sports teams to have been affected.

Duffy took to social media to provide the latest update on the nationwide ground stop: “The @FAAnews issued a nationwide ground stop for all U.S. airports following a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers. FAA technicians are investigating the issue.

We will provide immediate updates as we have them.”

Sunday’s matchup against No. 1 South Carolina was slated to be the Trojans’ biggest challenge of the season yet.

But USC women’s basketball will have to find a way to travel to the East Coast before taking the floor against the Gamecocks.

پوشش خبری بیشتر ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. قرار بود تیم بسکتبال زنان USC روز جمعه برای بازی بسیار پرطرفدار خود در برابر تیم Gamecocks، روز یکشنبه، به گرین‌ویل، کارولینای جنوبی برسد. اما این تیم به دلیل توقف پروازهای سراسری در تمام فرودگاه‌های ایالات متحده توسط اداره هوانوردی فدرال، در لس‌آنجلس زمین‌گیر شد. به‌روزرسانی: ما به دلیل توقف پروازهای سراسری، طبق اعلام FAA، در لس‌آنجلس زمین‌گیر شده‌ایم. به محض دریافت اطلاعات جدید، آنها را اعلام خواهیم کرد. حساب رسانه‌های اجتماعی تیم بیانیه زیر را در مورد این حادثه غیرمنتظره منتشر کرد: «به دستور FAA، پس از توقف پروازها در سراسر کشور، ما در لس‌آنجلس زمین‌گیر شده‌ایم. به محض دریافت اطلاعات جدید، آنها را اعلام خواهیم کرد.»
تیم فوتبال USC پیش از بازی روز شنبه مقابل ایندیانا در ورزشگاه مموریال، وارد بلومینگتون شد. شان دافی، نماینده کنگره ایالات متحده وزیر حمل‌ونقل روز جمعه اعلام کرد که FAA «توقف پروازها در سراسر کشور را برای همه فرودگاه‌های ایالات متحده» صادر کرده است که بر سفرهای چندین تیم ورزشی که برای بازی‌های آخر هفته عازم بودند، تأثیر گذاشته است. تیم بسکتبال زنان USC یکی از چندین تیم ورزشی دانشگاهی یا حرفه‌ای است که تحت تأثیر این موضوع قرار گرفته است. دافی در شبکه‌های اجتماعی آخرین اخبار مربوط به توقف پروازها در سراسر کشور را اعلام کرد: «@FAAnews توقف پروازها در سراسر کشور را برای همه فرودگاه‌های ایالات متحده صادر کرده است. فرودگاه‌ها به دنبال یک مشکل ارتباطی که بر همه مراکز کنترل ترافیک مسیر هوایی تأثیر گذاشته است. تکنسین‌های FAA در حال بررسی این مشکل هستند. به محض دریافت اطلاعات جدید، آنها را فوراً اعلام خواهیم کرد.»

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

A plaque honoring the Silicon Valley Denny’s where Jensen Huang famously founded Nvidia in 1993 is now gone – just a day after the chip titan resigned as CEO following reports he had multiple affairs.

The plaque sat above the booth that Huang and two of his co-founders – Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem – occupied when they conjured up what would become the key driver of today’s artificial intelligence boom.

“The booth that launched a $1 trillion company,” the inscription read in all-caps.

Now, only an empty patch of brick wall and chipped paint are left, according to an NBC News report, which noted two employees said the plaque had been removed.

When asked over the phone if Denny’s or someone else had removed the plaque, an employee at the San Jose, Calif. diner told The Post that she couldn’t provide any details.

The plaque was installed during a 2023 ceremony in which Huang – who said he washed dishes and waited tables in a Portland, Ore., Denny’s when he was 15 years old – met with Denny’s CEO at the time, Kelli Valade. They reminisced about Nvidia’s founding story during their confab.

Huang said he and his co-founders met at a booth near the back of the Denny’s to discuss creating a chip that would enable realistic 3-D graphics on personal computers. The Denny’s is roughly 8 miles from Nvidia’s headquarters.

“It had all the coffee you could drink and no one could chase you out,” Huang told Valade, according to an Nvidia blog post about the ceremony.

In the wake of Huang’s exit, passersby left flowers and bags of potato chips — a nod to the semiconductor chips that Nvidia builds – outside the company’s headquarters in Santa Clara, according to reports. Getty Images depicted a man placing a candle in front of an Nvidia sign.

Huang was forced to resign following a torrent of allegations in recent weeks over his conduct while at the helm of Nvidia.

The tech titan fessed last week to an affair with alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang, no relation.

Huang also faced allegations that he had an affair with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of health care — an exec who reports to him, the New York Times reported Wednesday.

Reuters reported Thursday that Huang had an intimate relationship with a second Nvidia employee, citing unnamed sources. Her name and other details were not known.

Colette Kress, Nvidia’s chief financial officer and executive vice president, is serving as interim CEO. Kress has been with the company for 13 years and will also continue to serve in her current roles during the search for a permanent replacement, which will consider both internal and external candidates.
news.content: در نتایج جست‌وجوی خود، پوشش خبری بیشتر ما را مشاهده کنید. تابلویی که به افتخار رستوران Denny's در سیلیکون‌ولی نصب شده بود، جایی که جنسن هوانگ به طور معروف در سال 1993 شرکت Nvidia را تأسیس کرد، اکنون ناپدید شده است - فقط یک روز پس از اینکه این غول تراشه‌سازی به دنبال گزارش‌هایی مبنی بر داشتن روابط نامشروع متعدد، از سمت مدیرعاملی استعفا داد. این لوح بالای غرفه‌ای قرار داشت که هوانگ و دو نفر از بنیانگذاران مشترک او - کریس مالاکوفسکی و کورتیس پریم - در آن حضور داشتند و در آنجا ایده‌ای را مطرح کردند که بعدها به عامل اصلی رونق هوش مصنوعی امروزی تبدیل شد.روی این لوح با حروف بزرگ نوشته شده بود: «غرفه‌ای که شرکتی با ارزش 1 تریلیون دلار را راه‌اندازی کرد.» اکنون، طبق گزارش NBC News، تنها یک قسمت خالی از دیوار آجری و رنگ‌بریده باقی مانده است. در این گزارش ذکر شده که دو کارمند گفته‌اند این لوح برداشته شده است. وقتی از طریق تلفن از یک کارمند رستوران دِنیز در سن‌خوزه، کالیفرنیا پرسیده شد که آیا دِنیز یا شخص دیگری لوح را برداشته است، او به The Post گفت که نمی‌تواند هیچ جزئیاتی ارائه دهد. این لوح در مراسمی در سال 2023 نصب شد که در آن هوانگ - که گفته بود در رستوران Denny's در پورتلند، اورگان، ظرف می‌شست و پیشخدمت بود -در رستوران Denny's در پورتلند، اورگان کار می‌کرد – با مدیرعامل وقت Denny's، کلی والاد، ملاقات کرد. آنها در طول گفت‌وگوی خود خاطراتی از داستان تأسیس Nvidia را مرور کردند. هوانگ گفت که او و شرکای مؤسسش در یک میز در نزدیکی قسمت پشتی رستوران Denny's دور هم جمع شدند تا درباره ساخت تراشه‌ای که امکان نمایش گرافیک سه‌بعدی واقع‌گرایانه را در رایانه‌های شخصی فراهم کند، گفتگو کنند. رستوران دنیز تقریباً 8 مایل با دفتر مرکزی انویدیا فاصله دارد.هوانگ طبق یک گزارش به والاد گفت: «هر چقدر قهوه می‌خواستی می‌توانستی بخوری و هیچ‌کس نمی‌توانست تو را بیرون کند.»

Craig Carton is mad … again.

Kirk Herbstreit is the target of his ire this time as the longtime ESPN college football analyst and pundit visited an NYC-based restaurant alongside his dog, Peter, a golden retriever with whom he travels.

Herbstreit posted a video on Instagram of him cutting up a steak to feed the dog off the plate.

Herbstreit added a stopwatch, and Peter ate an entire plate of cut-up steak in under 17 seconds.

“I wish he’d enjoy it,” Herbstreit said in the video. “I wish he’d go one bite at a time.”

Carton, unsurprisingly, had something to say.

“I’m not anti-dog. I just don’t want to go to a steakhouse and eat next to a dog. Because it’s disgusting,” Carton said on his show Friday.

“‘I love my dog more than you love your dog,'” Carton added. “You look to your right, and a beautifully cooked medium-rare steak is delivered to the Herbstreit table, but it’s not for any of the adults at that table, it’s for his dog. And Kirk, on camera now — because you’ve got to document everything you do, God forbid you act like a human being and you don’t film every aspect of your life — in a New York City steakhouse.

“While you’re getting ready to have a nice meal, the one you work your ass off for, ’cause you get to go out maybe once a week, and enjoy a nice meal with your wife, with another couple; now you’re sharing your meal with a dog.”

Herbstreit has been traveling with Peter for the past few years after his beloved dog — and previous travel companion — Ben died in November 2024.
news.content:
در نتایج جستجوی خود، پوشش خبری بیشتری از ما را ببینید. کریگ کارتون عصبانی است … باز هم. این بار هدف خشم او کرک هربرستریت است، تحلیلگر و کارشناس قدیمی فوتبال کالج ESPN که به همراه سگش، پیتر، یک گلدن رتریور که با او سفر می‌کند، از یک رستوران در نیویورک بازدید کرد. هربرستریت ویدیویی از خود در اینستاگرام منتشر کرد که در آن در حال برش استیک برای غذا دادن به سگ از بشقاب است. هربستریت یک کرنومتر اضافه کرد و پیتر یک بشقاب کامل استیک خرد شده را در کمتر از 17 ثانیه خورد.هربستریت در این ویدئو گفت: «کاش از آن لذت می‌برد.» «کاش هر بار یک لقمه می‌خورد.»
جای تعجب نیست که کارتون هم حرفی برای گفتن داشت.«من ضد سگ نیستم. فقط نمی‌خواهم به یک رستوران استیک بروم و کنار یک سگ غذا بخورم. چون این کار چندش‌آور است.» کارتون روز جمعه در برنامه خود گفت.کارتون افزود: «من سگم را بیشتر از شما که سگتان را دوست دارید، دوست دارم.» «به سمت راست خود نگاه می‌کنید و می‌بینید که یک استیک نیمه پخته شده زیبا به میز هربرستریت آورده می‌شود، اما این استیک برای هیچ‌یک از بزرگسالان حاضر در آن میز نیست، بلکه برای سگ اوست. و کرک، الان جلوی دوربین است — چون باید هر کاری که انجام می‌دهید را ثبت کنید، خدا نکند مثل یک انسان رفتار کنید و هر جنبه‌ای از زندگی‌تان را فیلم نگیرید — در یک رستوران استیک در شهر نیویورک. «وقتی داری آماده می‌شی تا یک غذای خوشمزه بخوری، همان غذایی که برایش خیلی زحمت می‌کشی، چون شاید هفته‌ای یک بار بتوانی بیرون بروی و از یک غذای خوشمزه با همسرت، با یک زوج دیگر لذت ببری؛ حالا داری غذایت را با یک سگ شریک می‌شوی.»
هربرستریت پس از فوت همسر محبوبش، چند سالی است که با پیتر سفر می‌کند.

Dejounte Murray has had enough of New Orleans.

The former All-Star requested a trade from the Pelicans, with his agent, Klutch Sports CEO Rich Paul, and team officials beginning to work toward finding him a new home, ESPN’s Shams Charania first reported.

The Pelicans then put out a statement and said they are looking into “potential trade options.”

“Today, Dejounte Murray’s representatives informed us of his request to be traded,” the Pelicans said in a statement shared on X. “We will evaluate potential trade opportunities that are in the best interest of our organization.”

The trade request comes less than two days after Murray took to social media to suggest there was “sabotage” going on behind the scenes with the team.

After the Pelicans’ blowout 145-111 home loss to the Nets on Wednesday, Murray took to X, pointing out that the team was 1-8 with him in the lineup this season and 3-0 without him.

“From what’s going on INSIDE, this sounds like someone hit you to say this!! THE ‘SABOTAGE’ IS REAL!!” Murray wrote in the since-deleted post.

Murray, 30, reposted Charania’s report on Friday afternoon.

At least one potential suitor has already emerged.

The Suns have expressed interest in acquiring Murray, per NBA insider Chris Haynes.

Murray has had a disastrous tenure with the franchise since he was traded by the Hawks in July 2024 for a package headlined by Dyson Daniels and two first-round picks.

Daniels has since emerged as one of the best perimeter defenders in the NBA, while Murray has appeared in just 54 games in a Pelicans uniform, suffering a fractured hand in his New Orleans debut before tearing his Achilles in January 2025.

The Pelicans, who hired Jamahl Mosley as their head coach during the offseason, have lost four straight games, including a 51-point drubbing at the hands of the Warriors on Monday.

Murray is making $32.8 million this season and holds a $30.8 million player option for the 2027-28 campaign after signing a $114-plus million veteran extension in 2023.

Republican Colorado Rep. Lauren Boebert lost her reelection bid two years after moving to one of the state’s reddest districts, The Associated Press reported Friday.

Boebert narrowly lost to Democratic Colorado Rep.-elect Eileen Laubacher after she moved districts to boost her reelection chances. The Republican congresswoman was an ally of President Donald Trump throughout most of her political career, although she broke with Trump over a petition to force a vote on releasing the Epstein Files.

Boebert won her 2022 race in Colorado’s third district by just 546 votes against then-Democratic Colorado congressional nominee Adam Frisch. The congresswoman then moved to the Fourth District in 2024 to avoid another close race.

Republican Colorado Rep.-elect Jeff Hurd won his seat in Colorado’s third district by a narrow two-point margin.

Laubacher served in the U.S. Navy for 34 years and campaigned on affordability and ending corruption, the two top issues in the election. Trump, his family and administration officials have been accused of several corrupt actions, including accepting a plane from Qatar and pardoning a cryptocurrency exchange CEO tied to Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump’s business ventures.

Democrats regained majorities in the House and Senate while voters soured on the economy and the Iran war. A slew of Republican-held seats flipped to Democrats, and many Democrats won seats in gerrymandered districts designed to help Republicans.

Trump attempted to pressure Boebert and Republican South Carolina Rep. Nancy Mace to remove their names from a discharge petition aimed at forcing a floor vote on releasing the Epstein files. She refused to remove her name.

Boebert endorsed Republican Kentucky Rep. Thomas Massie against his Trump-endorsed challenger ahead of his primary in May. She also praised Trump in the same statement, stating they had both fought to save the country. (RELATED: ‘F*ck You, First Of All’: Lauren Boebert Goes Off On Reporter When Asked About Alleged Affair With Thomas Massie)

“Below is my friend Thomas Massie. He loves America and is fighting to save it,” Boebert said. “Also below is my friend and President, Donald Trump. He’s put his life on the line to save this great country. I support both of these men. I’ve worked with both to preserve freedom and liberty. And if that makes you angry, bless your heart.”

The Colorado congresswoman was one of 19 Republicans in June to vote against a temporary extension of Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA), a warrantless spying tool.

Boebert faced several controversies throughout her time in Congress. A House Ethics complaint filed by American Muckrakers’ David Wheeler alleged that Boebert had sexual relationships with three staffers and arranged a $20,000 hush money payment. She denied the accusations and referred to the allegations as a “politically motivated stunt.”

Footage caught Boebert groping a male companion and vaping during a September 2023 production of Beetlejuice.

Boebert’s 21-year-old son, Tyler, was arrested in a child exploitation case in August.

news.originalContent:
Officials have not said if anyone was hurt after American Heritage was partially submerged with 129 passengers on board.

A tanker has struck a river cruise boat carrying 129 passengers on the Mississippi River in New Orleans, partially submerging the vessel and prompting a major rescue operation.

The Atlantic Asphalt tanker hit the American Heritage paddleboat on Friday at about 12:30pm local time (18:30 GMT), the Port of New Orleans said. The cruise boat had docked about two hours earlier to begin letting passengers off. The authorities have not released any information on injuries or deaths.

“Multiple individuals have been rescued, and search-and-rescue operations remain ongoing,” a city spokesperson said.

Video from the scene showed the much larger tanker hitting the paddlewheel cruise boat as metal and glass crashed and crunched, according to The Associated Press news agency.

More than a dozen people in life jackets were dragged from the river, where the water temperature was 19 degrees Celsius (66 degrees Fahrenheit), onto nearby ships, while others stood near the railing as the boat listed further into the water.

“Surreal, that’s what that was,” one witness, Jamie Holford, told local television. “Fifteen minutes from impact to where it rolled over.”

Port police, the fire department, the coastguard and emergency medical staff are on the scene, and a triage area was set up inside the port’s administration building. The river was closed to vessel traffic.

American Cruise Lines, which operates the boat, said guests and crew had been evacuated and that it was “deeply concerned for everyone involved”.

The five-deck American Heritage, built in 2015, holds up to 150 passengers and was finishing an eight-day cruise to destinations in Louisiana and Mississippi.

The 160-metre (520-foot) tanker was flying the flag of the Marshall Islands and was bound for New Orleans, according to the MarineTraffic tracker. It specialises in carrying asphalt and bitumen, according to the maritime periodical Marine Insights.

The cause of the collision, as well as whether the ship was carrying cargo, remains unknown.

news.originalContent:
US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy says federal aviation agency is ‘investigating the issue’.

The United States has grounded flights across the country after a “communication issue” impacted traffic control centres, US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said.

“FAA [Federal Aviation Administration] technicians are investigating the issue. We will provide immediate updates as we have them,” Duffy wrote on social media.

The FAA said in a post on X that there had been a “temporary telecommunications outage” and that, as a precaution, all flights were being halted. International flights would be handled case by case, it added.

About 7,000 flights have been either delayed or cancelled due to the stop, according to FlightAware.

Some 4,042 flights were in the air, heading to US airports, when the ground stop was ordered, according to the tracking site Flightradar24.

The communication issue affects all 22 Air Route Traffic Control Centers, which guide aircraft.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told reporters there was no indication that the ground stop was triggered by a threat to the US. “Everybody’s safe. The flights are accounted for,” he said. “This is not another 9/11.”

President Donald Trump had been briefed, he said.

Asked whether a planned rollout of a new AI tool meant to help air traffic controllers could be to blame, Mullin said officials had not ruled it out. “You just can’t rule out anything at this point. We are going through that process,” he said.

The FBI does not believe a cyberattack or criminal activity caused the failure, Bloomberg reported, citing an official familiar with the matter.

news.originalContent:
The Chicago-born pope was welcomed by huge crowds in the coastal city, on the final leg of his South America tour.

Pope Leo has made an emotional return to his former diocese of Chiclayo in Peru, where large crowds welcomed their former bishop exactly one month after he had lung cancer surgery, and he thanked them for their support during his recovery.

“As I look at your faces, a prayer of thanksgiving to the Lord arises in my heart for the blessing you have been and continue to be in my life,” he said.

About 500,000 people gathered for Mass at Pampas de Pimentel, a desert park just outside of Peru’s fourth-largest city, according to estimates from the Vatican, while another million lined his motorcade route.

Before he was elected pope, Leo had spent about two decades working in Peru as a missionary priest and served as bishop of Chiclayo, where he is still known as “Padre Roberto” and where his image is ubiquitous, from 2015 to 2023.

In Chiclayo, a coastal city of about 620,000, Leo earned a reputation for staying close to poor communities during times of crisis, including when the region was hit with devastating floods and the COVID-19 pandemic.

Some had camped overnight to see him, while others walked in the hot sun to avoid bumper-to-bumper traffic to get to the open-air Mass.

As he rode in his popemobile, people in the crowd waved yellow and white Vatican flags and shouted, “The pope is from Chiclayo.”

“What a joy it is to return to Chiclayo,” said Leo at the start of his homily.

Originally from Chicago and formerly known as Robert Francis Prevost, Leo also holds Peruvian citizenship and declared the country his homeland on Wednesday.

Peru is the final stop of his 12-day, three-country South America tour, coming after visits to Argentina and Uruguay. Approximately 12 million people have come to see him at public events so far.

Last month, he underwent surgery for lung cancer, amid fears that the trip would have to be cancelled. But doctors have said the cancer was localised, had not spread, and would not require further treatment.

Leo will stay in the Chiclayo area until Sunday, leading eight events, including a private dinner with the priests he oversaw during his time as bishop.

news.originalContent:
The criminal association charge over his alleged role in the collapse of the bank comes a week after his removal.

Paraguayan prosecutors have charged former president Santiago Pena with criminal association over his alleged role in the collapse of the digital bank Ueno, a week after Congress removed him from office.

The prosecutor’s office announced the new charge on Friday, adding to the breach of trust and self-dealing charges already facing Pena, who is being held in pretrial detention at a military facility.

The 47-year-old former leader is accused of using his position to direct millions in government funds to Ueno and concealing or downplaying its financial troubles, despite warnings of risky lending practices, while having financial ties to the bank.

Pena, who entered office in 2023, held a stake in the bank’s holding company until last year.

On Thursday, investigators raided his official residence in the capital, Asuncion. The prosecutor’s office said agents from the economic crimes unit were extracting data and gathering relevant information for the investigation.

Last week, Pena tried to step down as president, but Congress rejected his resignation, instead removing him from office through impeachment. Pena was arrested shortly after his removal.

The collapse of Ueno left customers locked out of their accounts, prompting huge protests across the country as thousands demanded accountability and their money back.

Prosecutors had been looking for missing funds and said on Friday that assets had been located abroad, although they did not specify in which countries. They had previously asked the United States, Luxembourg and Argentina for help locating the missing money.

“The necessary steps are under way to request that they be frozen,” prosecutor Francisco Cabrera told reporters.

Three former central bank officials were also arrested on Friday, accused of having known about Ueno’s issues since late last year.

The bank, which held more than $800m in public funds, grew quickly under Pena’s presidency from a financial technology company into a large firm handling state pensions and the accounts of several government entities.

The credit ratings agency Fitch has placed Paraguay’s sovereign rating on watch for a possible downgrade, which would make it more expensive for the government to borrow money.

On Thursday, the Central Bank said it had returned savings to more than 1.8 million people who had deposited money at the bank.

(Photo by Drew Angerer/Getty Images)

Former Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) Director John Brennan’s son was arrested by the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Friday on charges related to child pornography, a law enforcement source confirmed to the Daily Caller.

Brennan’s 40-year-old son Kyle was arrested by the bureau and charged with knowingly transporting child pornography using a means or facility of interstate or foreign commerce, the Caller learned. Kyle was charged in the Eastern District of Virginia. (RELATED: Feds Raid Beverly Hills Mansion In Connection To Disgraced Dem Eric Swalwell)

The FBI did not respond to a request for comment from the Daily Caller.

An affidavit viewed by the Daily Caller, states Kyle Brennan used an Adobe product tied to his Apple ID to upload child sex abuse material (CSAM), including an image “depicting the lascivious exhibition of a pubescent minor.”

The image, referred to as “File-1,” the affidavit alleges, “File-1 appears to be a morphed image, combining the face of a minor girl (lateridentified as’ MVr’) and the naked body of a different minor girl. The focus of the image is the minor’s genitals, which are pushed forward toward the camera. The girl whose body is shown in the image appears to be in the early stages of puberty… .”

“According to records WPD [Warrenton Police Department] obtained from Comcast, the IP address used to upload the suspected child pornography files to Adobe was registered to Kyle BRENNAN at an address in Warrenton. Virginia,” the affidavit states.

According to the Daily Mail, which was the first to report the story, the FBI seized and searched Brennan’s cellular phone Thursday evening. The Mail states that federal agents found nearly 90 images of CSAM on Kyle Brennan’s phone, including a photo of a “fully nude pubescent minor girl on a locker bench.”

The former CIA director is himself a potential subject of a criminal investigation from President Donald Trump’s administration over his role in the Russiagate conspiracy. (RELATED: Former CIA Director John Brennan Subpoenaed Over Russiagate Conspiracy Against Trump)

In addition to Brennan, the Trump administration has pursued legal action against various political adversaries and officials, including Democratic Minnesota Rep. Ilhan Omar, former FBI Director James Comey, and New York Attorney General Letitia James.

news.originalContent:
(Photo by Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images)

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent shifted blame onto Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and his department Friday for failing to blacklist Megaspeed, the company at the center of the scandal surrounding former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and his alleged affair with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset.

While speaking on CNBC’s Squawk Box, Bessent said the U.S. Trade Representative and the Departments of the Treasury, War, and State all supported placing Megaspeed on the Entity List. The list is a trade blacklist for foreign businesses, research institutions, government organizations, and individuals considered at risk of involvement in activities contrary to U.S. national security or foreign policy interests. (RELATED: Trump: ‘There’s Only One Man’ To Replace Ousted Nvidia CEO)

However, Bessent said Lutnick’s Department of Commerce has the final say over who joins the list, adding that “you will have to ask them about their internal process.”

U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent blames Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick over Nvidia chip mess: "Treasury, War, USTR and State were in favor of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months." https://t.co/0BTlHymwUY

The interview followed an Axios report that Bessent had asked Lutnick why he hesitated to place export controls on businesses like Megaspeed, which had shipped Nvidia’s advanced AI chips to China.

A Commerce Department spokesperson denied that the conversation took place. However, Bessent said that “We don’t repeat conversations in the Situation Room,” CNBC reported.

“I am frustrated when President Trump made it very clear that China should not receive any Nvidia chips above H100S,” Bessent said, regarding potential delays in export controls. He added that “any leakage is very frustrating” because it “hurts our great companies in the AI race [and] gives the Chinese an advantage.”

(L-R) U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick look on as U.S. President Donald Trump prepares to sign executive orders in the Oval Office of the White House on April 09, 2025 in Washington, DC. (Photo by Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

The controversy erupted after reports emerged that Huang had been shipping chips to China following an alleged romantic relationship with Alice Huang, the former CEO of Singaporean tech company Megaspeed, who has allegedly doubled as a spy for China.

Alice allegedly used her ties with Huang to help move at least $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia chips to Chinese tech firms since 2023, The Information reported.

When asked whether the processors had made it to China through Megaspeed, Bessent said, “I think that there is a lot of leakage in the system, and we are constantly working to close that down.”

U.S. President Donald Trump (R) greets Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, as Trump and AI executives hold a media briefing following a meeting on artificial intelligence outside the West Wing of the White House on September 29, 2026 in Washington, DC. (Photo by Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images)

“The story has been thus far on Jensen Huang’s personal foibles,” Bessent continued on CNBC. “The real story here should be: Did Nvidia know their client, and was there a robust effort at Nvidia to make sure that there was no leakage and that they were selling to what were obviously pass-through shell companies?”

The Departments of the Treasury and Commerce, as well as the White House, did not respond to the Daily Caller’s request for comment.

When asked whether the processors had made it to China through Megaspeed, Bessent said, “I think that there is a lot of leakage in the system, and we are constantly working to close that down.”

“The story has been thus far on Jensen Huang’s personal foibles,” Bessent continued on CNBC. “The real story here should be: Did Nvidia know their client, and was there a robust effort at Nvidia to make sure that there was no leakage and that they were selling to what were obviously pass-through shell companies?”

The Departments of the Treasury and Commerce, as well as the White House, did not respond to the Daily Caller’s request for comment.

Photo Illustration by Daily Caller Staff; source images by Oliver Contreras / AFP via Getty ; Martin Barraud / Getty ; Kevin Dietsch/Getty ; Andrew Harnik/Getty ; antonbrand/ Getty; Kevin Carter/Getty

Following the midterm elections, Republicans face mounting pressure to advance what is being characterized as amnesty for illegal immigrant agricultural workers during the remaining time they control the House.

Having campaigned heavily on cracking down on illegal immigration in 2024, GOP lawmakers now face renewed scrutiny over whether they will follow through on those promises before potentially losing their House majority — or if they will cave to special interests and pass an immigration reform plan that includes some form of amnesty. (RELATED: EXCLUSIVE: White House Scrambles After Trump Again Floats Amnesty Deal With Democrats)

A bipartisan immigration proposal still simmering on Capitol Hill is once again drawing attention after recent remarks from President Donald Trump and Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, who have signaled willingness to work with Democrats on immigration reform.

Wrong. The word “amnesty” was never even said in this entire exchange.

The legislation, sponsored by Republican Pennsylvania Rep. Glenn (GT) Thompson, chairman of the House Agriculture Committee, is known as the Securing Agriculture’s Workforce Act of 2026 (SAWA). The bill would in effect grant amnesty to illegal immigrants who work in the agricultural sector.

Introduced by Thompson in June 2025, the legislation remains pending in the House Judiciary Committee, where it awaits further action from Chairman Jim Jordan, the next Republican House minority leader.

AmericanHort, a national horticulture industry association, confirmed to the Caller that it sent a letter to the House Judiciary Committee urging Jordan to work with Thompson to advance SAWA.

The organization, which represents the plant and horticultural industry, has also published the letter on its website, calling on lawmakers to address H-2A wage and program issues following a recent California ruling affecting the Department of Labor’s October 2025 interim final rule.

Thompson’s bill also seeks to address agricultural labor shortages by allowing eligible illegal immigrant farmworkers to obtain special immigration status and legally remain in the U.S. while continuing to work in qualifying agricultural jobs.

Specifically, the legislation would extend eligibility to illegal immigrants who performed at least six months of qualifying agricultural work within the previous two years.

It would also waive certain grounds of inadmissibility, creating a pathway for eligible workers to obtain H-2A visa status and legally remain in the country while continuing to work in the agricultural industry.

Jeremy Beck, co-president of NumbersUSA, and Mark Krikorian, executive director of the Center for Immigration Studies, both told the Daily Caller that the proposal amounts to amnesty for illegal immigrants, arguing that it would grant legal status to individuals based on their prior agricultural employment.

Notably, the Federation for American Immigration Reform (FAIR) defines amnesty as the “granting of legal status to any individual who is in the country illegally.”

Rep. Thompson also expressed optimism about the legislation’s prospects during a panel hosted by the American Dairy Coalition at the World Dairy Expo in Madison, Wisconsin, on Oct. 30, saying he hoped Congress would address both SAWA and the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026 during the lame-duck session.

During the discussion, Thompson highlighted the agricultural industry’s alleged longstanding labor challenges, particularly the lack of a year-round visa program for dairy farms. (RELATED: EXCLUSIVE: Trump ‘Will Never Allow For Mass Amnesty’ After Floating Working With Dems On Immigration)

However, when asked by the Caller about the possibility of Republicans advancing Thompson’s legislation during the lame-duck session, Beck warned that doing so could further take the wind out of Republican voters’ already frayed sails.

“Pushing something like this in the lame duck would send a terrible message to an already demoralized electorate,” Beck told Caller, arguing that Republicans won control of Congress by campaigning on prioritizing American workers over illegal immigration.

Beck added that the midterm elections offered no indication that voters had abandoned that message, but rather that immigration had taken a back seat to other issues, ranking a “distant third” among the issues influencing the results.

At its core, Thompson’s legislation seeks to address employers’ labor needs by providing a legal workforce for temporary agricultural jobs through the H-2A program.

The program allows U.S. employers or authorized agents to bring foreign nationals into the country for temporary agricultural work, subject to specific regulatory requirements, according to the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) website.

The proposal would cap annual increases to the Adverse Effect Wage Rate (AEWR), the minimum wage employers must pay certain H-2A workers, at 3.25 percent.

The cap could constrain wage growth for both foreign and domestic agricultural workers covered by the rate. This cap, opponents argue, acts as a means to suppress agricultural worker wages. Notably, labor market data shows prevailing farm wages have risen faster than the proposed threshold.

When the Caller asked Krikorian about the legislation’s potential long-term effects, he forewarned that its passage could preserve outdated agricultural practices instead of incentivizing the industry to modernize and reduce its reliance on foreign labor.

“Why in the 21st century are we having people kneel in the dirt and pull plants out with their hands? What kind of thing is that? This is medieval,” Krikorian told the Caller.

Furthermore, Krikorian argues that illegal immigration, guest worker programs and legislation like SAWA “preserve the feudalistic nature of much of American agriculture” by allowing the industry to rely on foreign labor rather than encouraging technological advancements that could reduce the need for imported workers.

The proposal comes amid a broader history of Republican lawmakers pursuing immigration deals with Democrats, including the bipartisan border and immigration reform package negotiated in early 2024 by Republican Oklahoma Sen. James Lankford, who is now seeking to become the top Republican on the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee (HSGAC).

When asked by the Caller about Lankford seeking the ranking member position on the committee, Republican strategist Ryan Girdusky wrote, “Lankford sucks on immigration.”

Lankford was the front man for the disastrous amnesty bill the GOP establishment tried to get us to swallow a few years ago. Needs to be watched like a hawk.

Lankford is not the only Republican to have pursued immigration compromises with Democrats. Former Florida Sen. and current Secretary of State Marco Rubio, the late Arizona Sen. John McCain, and former President George W. Bush have also supported efforts to reach bipartisan immigration deals.

The issue resurfaced Tuesday when Fox News’ The Ingraham Angle host Laura Ingraham challenged Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin over his openness to working with Democrats. (RELATED: ‘Why Did You Float DACA?’: Mullin Put On The Spot Over Immigration Deal)

Ingraham put Mullin on the spot, arguing that Republicans repeatedly turn to immigration compromises when facing political difficulties, despite what she described as Democrats’ lack of interest in lowering immigration levels or enforcing existing laws.

🚨 JUST NOW: Laura Ingraham DESTROYS Markwayne Miullin LIVE ON FOX for pushing for "LEGAL STATUS" for DACA illegals LAURA: "Why would ANY idea be floated to work with the Democrats on an issue that is their HOLY GRAIL?!" "It seems like EVERY TIME Republicans feel like they’re running into a rough spot, they rush to some type of immigration deal with a party that you yourself has said has NO INTEREST in lowering immigration, legal immigration, or enforcing the laws as they exist." "Why did you float DACA, Mr. Secretary? Why is THAT the message for you guys this election?!" — @IngrahamAngle MULLIN: "… some of them may not even speak English or never even lived in their country!" WHAT KIND OF ARGUMENT IS THAT?! NO AMNESTY. PERIOD.

Krikorian argued that immigration policy within the Republican Party is ultimately driven from the top down, placing responsibility for the party’s direction on the president. He told the Caller that “ultimately, the responsibility does stop with” Trump, adding, “I think he believes this stuff, too. I don’t think. I know he does.”

At the same time, Krikorian characterized Trump as a transitional figure on immigration, arguing that the president largely adheres to the conventional Republican position that “legal [immigration] good, illegal bad,” while demonstrating a willingness to devote resources to enforcing immigration laws.

Looking beyond Trump’s presidency, Krikorian suggested that the next generation of Republican leaders, including Vice President JD Vance, Florida Republican Gov. Ron DeSantis and potentially Rubio, may be more inclined to embrace a broader restrictionist approach focused on reducing immigration overall.

Trump’s recent personnel changes and public statements have also brought the administration’s immigration direction into focus.

On Nov. 6, Trump announced that Wiles would be leaving her position after submitting her resignation Thursday night, with Stephen Miller, one of the administration’s most prominent immigration hardliners and a key architect of Trump’s immigration agenda, set to succeed her. (RELATED: Trump Taps Top Immigration Adviser As New Chief Of Staff)

Just hours before the announcement, Trump reiterated his opposition to amnesty in an interview with “60 Minutes,” while also signaling a willingness to work with Democrats on immigration reform.

He struck a similar tone during Monday’s press briefing, again reaffirming his opposition to amnesty while expressing openness to bipartisan negotiations.

President Trump says there will be no amnesty: Reporter: "Mr. President, you told 60 Minutes that you felt your deportation policy may have gone too far. But then you named the architect of that policy, Stephen Miller to be your Chief of Staff. Have you told him that you want changes to the deportation policy?" President Trump: "No. We have a very strong deportation policy. There is no amnesty. No anything. We keep that. But we focus on the worst of the worst."

However, when asked by the Caller whether immigration reform could be pursued without amnesty, Beck cautioned that “the devil’s always in the details.” He argued that allowing someone who is in the country illegally to remain in the U.S., regardless of what the policy is called, “that’s an amnesty.”

The current debate echoes one that raged in the first Trump administration, when Republican lawmakers repeatedly faced pressure to strike bipartisan immigration deals, often invoking labor shortages and proposals to provide certain undocumented immigrants with a pathway to remain in the country.

Now, following Republican losses in the midterm elections, similar questions are resurfacing over whether the party will once again pursue a bipartisan immigration deal.

When asked by the Caller whether congressional Republicans should use the remaining lame-duck session to advance SAWA or similar immigration reform legislation, Jeremy Carl, a senior fellow at the Claremont Institute and former Trump administration nominee for assistant secretary of state, warned that doing so could carry significant political consequences, likening the move to the fate of General George Custer.

“If the GOP Congress passes stealth amnesty to benefit multi-billion-dollar Big Ag [agriculture] corporations — in the wake of an election in which immigration was the one issue on which voters preferred the GOP, they’d be committing the biggest strategic mistake since Gen. Custer took on the Sioux at the Battle of Little Bighorn,” Carl wrote.
